hints.S44_A1: The result tells you everything: THE MIXTURE WAS LIGHT AND FLUFFY after the BUTTER AND SUGAR were beaten together. Ask: which verb names that beating step? 'Dissolved' belongs to sugar in liquid, not to butter.
hints.S44_A2: FLOUR is a fine powder, spread in a light layer TO PREVENT THE DOUGH FROM STICKING. Ask: which verb means to sprinkle a fine powder evenly over a surface? 'Poured' belongs to liquids.
hints.S44_A3: The dough is left UNDISTURBED IN THE FRIDGE OVERNIGHT so that the LAYERS BECOME FLAKY. Ask: which verb means to leave food alone so that it improves? 'Melt' and 'dissolve' would ruin it completely.
hints.S44_A4: The crust is GOLDEN and the whole KITCHEN SMELLS WONDERFUL - this loaf came out well. Ask: which adjective means pleasantly firm and crunchy? 'Soggy' and 'raw' would mean the baking failed.
hints.S44_A5: The dash proves it: EACH ONE PRECISE TO THE NEAREST GRAM. Ask: which adjective means extremely careful about every detail? 'Vague', 'approximate' and 'imprecise' all mean the opposite.
hints.S44_B1: HAS is already in place, and FOR OVER THIRTY YEARS runs right up to today. Ask: after 'has', which form completes a present perfect? 'Use' is a regular verb, so its past participle is easy to build.
hints.S44_B2: SHE NOTICED the temperature - a sudden discovery cutting into a longer action. Ask: which choice shows the work already under way at that past moment? A one-word past form would end it too early.
hints.S44_B3: THAN compares just two loaves, and 'good' refuses to take -er. Ask: what is the comparative of 'good'? GOODER is never English, and 'the best' would need three or more loaves.
hints.S44_B4: SUGAR cannot be counted - there is no plural - and THAN sets this recipe against what I expected: ONLY TWO TABLESPOONS. Ask: which quantity word lowers an uncountable amount? 'Fewer' needs things you can count.
hints.S44_B5: The statement is POSITIVE and sits in the past: the oven WAS PREHEATED. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag flip to negative or stay positive? The tag keeps the same tense, so a present form is out.
hints.S44_B6: JUST is the giveaway: homemade cookies and the BOUTIQUE BAKERIES' ones are equally DELICIOUS, neither better nor worse. Ask: which pair of words builds an EQUAL comparison?
hints.S44_B7: The CAKE did not bake itself: A FOURTEEN-YEAR-OLD did, and the COMPETITION is over. Ask: which choice is passive, with the subject receiving the action, and set firmly in the past?
hints.S44_B8: The instructor is FORBIDDING something, warning that THE DOUGH would BECOME TOUGH. Ask: after 'told + person', does a plain verb follow, an -ing form, or an infinitive with its marker? And where does the negative word sit?
hints.S44_C1: ENJOYS is the deciding word. Ask: after 'enjoy', 'love' or 'keep', which form of the verb must follow - a plain one, an infinitive, or one ending in -ing? Grandma is not planning; she is doing what she likes.
hints.S44_C2: SHE is one person, the habit is regular (EVERY SATURDAY MORNING), and nothing here is finished past time. Ask: in the simple present, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one carrying -s?
hints.S44_C3: LAST SUNDAY is finished time, and this is one completed action, not one in progress. Ask: which single-word past form fits? A continuous form would need a helper standing in front of it.
hints.S44_C4: WHILE tells you this action stretched on until THE KITCHEN FILLED with the scent - it had not finished. Ask: which past continuous form suits a SINGULAR subject like Grandma? A one-word past form would end it too soon.
hints.S44_C5: HER GRANDCHILDREN is plural, and AT THE SAME TIME points back to Grandma's ongoing action. Ask: which past continuous form partners a plural subject? Check the helper before you choose.
hints.S44_C6: WANTS is the deciding word. Ask: after 'want', 'hope' or 'decide', does the verb take -ing, or an infinitive with its little marker in front? Compare blank 1, where ENJOYS behaves differently.
hints.S44_C7: SHOULD is a modal, and modals never let their verb take an ending. Ask: after 'should', 'must' or 'can', does the verb add -s, add -ing, or add nothing at all?
hints.S44_C8: RIGHT NOW means at this very moment, so the action has not finished. Ask: which present continuous form partners a singular subject like Grandma? A simple present would turn it into a weekly habit instead.
hints.S44_D1: The dash lists them: FLOUR AND BUTTER, EGGS AND VANILLA, each with A SPECIFIC ROLE. Ask: which box word names any single item that goes into a recipe? 'Batch' counts finished goods, not what goes in.
hints.S44_D2: The clue follows the blank: agents that CAUSE DOUGH AND BATTER TO RISE BY PRODUCING BUBBLES OF GAS, such as BAKING POWDER AND YEAST. Ask: which box word names that kind of agent?
hints.S44_D3: The blank follows 'require the baker to', so it must be a plain verb, and the clue is PRESSING AND FOLDING IT REPEATEDLY WITH THE HANDS. Ask: which box word names that action?
hints.S44_D4: The clue is A LARGE ORDER and MANY ITEMS prepared in one go TO SAVE TIME. Ask: which box word names one round of baking that produces many items together?
hints.S44_D5: The clue follows the dash: THE SMELL OF WARM BUTTER AND SUGAR that FILLS THE KITCHEN. Ask: which box word names a lovely smell? 'Crust' is something you can touch, not something you breathe in.
hints.S44_E1: Count the subject: THE CROISSANTS - more than one, sitting in the oven. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular past verb, or the plural one? Never match the verb to 'the oven'.
hints.S44_E2: FOLDED is an action verb, and the underlined word tells you HOW the baker folded the DOUGH. Ask: does an action take an adjective, or an adverb? Adjectives belong to nouns.
hints.S44_E3: Test it: WE STOOD ___ NEAR THE LARGE MIXING COUNTER - can you say 'at that place'? Nobody owns anything in this sentence. Ask: which spelling names a place, and which means 'belonging to them'?
hints.S44_E4: ONE baker owns that CLEAN WHITE APRON, and the underlined word carries no apostrophe at all. Ask: can a plain -s ever show ownership? Where must the apostrophe go when there is a single owner?
hints.S44_E5: SHELF ends in -f, and the WOODEN ones by the window are more than one. Ask: how do you write more than one leaf, or more than one loaf? Apply that same change here - a plain -s will not do.
hints.S44_F1: Sentence A sets the condition: you FOLLOW THE RECIPE PRECISELY. Ask: after a condition phrase, may the verb take 'will', or must it stay in the simple present? Keep the future for the promise in the second half.
hints.S44_F2: Both sentences describe THE CROISSANTS, so name them once and let 'which' carry the second mention. Ask: after 'which', is the word 'they' still needed? And which punctuation marks fence off the extra information?
